# Polyglot Codebase Knowledge Graph

> Generated offline by **readmenator**. 159 files, 3110 symbols, 1363 imports. Supports C, C++, Python, Go, Rust, JS/TS, Java, C#, Shell, PHP, Dart, GDScript, Nim, ASM, Ruby, Swift, Kotlin, Scala, Lua, Elixir.
> No LLMs. No tokens. Pure static analysis. See more [here](https://github.com/grisuno/ReadMenator)

**Start here:** Statistics Dashboard for scope, God Nodes for blast radius, Architecture Reference for per-file API. Agents: prefer `readmenator-agent/INDEX.md` + `SYMBOLS.md`.

**Wiki:** prefer `readmenator-wiki/index.md` for progressive disclosure: one synthesis page per community, `connections.json` with EXTRACTED vs INFERRED confidence, `queries.md` log, `REPORT.md` audit.

**Confidence:** EXTRACTED = parsed from source, INFERRED = heuristic bridge, AMBIGUOUS = reported, never hidden. See `readmenator-wiki/REPORT.md`.

**Total Files Parsed:** 159 | **Total Symbols Extracted:** 3110 | **Total Imports:** 1363
 | **Resolved Imports:** 621

## Architecture Overview

8 components stacked in 6 dependency tiers (weighted Eades-Lin-Smyth ordering: arrows point from dependent to dependency, top to bottom). Labels are import counts, thick arrows the top quartile; 12 transitively implied edges are omitted. Dashed red arrows are upward dependencies: the smallest set of imports that closes every cycle and breaks the layering. Cyan components hold entry points. Interactive version: `readmenator-apidocs/index.html#/flows`.

Upward dependencies to fix first: `readmenator/parsers` -> `readmenator: _video` (6 imports); `readmenator: _video` -> `readmenator: _flowcharts` (6 imports); `readmenator: _diagrams` -> `readmenator: _video` (6 imports); `readmenator: _video` -> `readmenator: _graphrag` (5 imports); `readmenator: _video` -> `readmenator: _agent_output` (4 imports); `readmenator: _video` -> `readmenator: _pipeline` (3 imports); `readmenator: _diagrams` -> `readmenator: _agent_output` (3 imports); `readmenator: _graphrag` -> `readmenator: _pipeline` (2 imports); `readmenator/parsers` -> `readmenator: _graphrag` (1 imports); `readmenator: _diagrams` -> `readmenator: _graphrag` (1 imports)

## Query Recipes

Example queries you can run against this knowledge base using the ranking engine:

```
# Find files most relevant to a concept
readmenator query "Where is the import resolver implemented?"

# Rank files by relevance to a topic
readmenator query "How does documentation generation work?"

# Explain why a file ranks highly
readmenator query "explain readmenator/_documentation.py"

# Trace dependency paths with ranked context
readmenator query "path from CLI to exporter"
```

The ranking model uses the following signals:

- **Personalized PageRank** (45% weight): query-specific relevance via seed propagation
- **Global Authority** (20% weight): structural importance via standard PageRank
- **Test Coverage** (15% weight): fraction of symbols referenced in test files
- **Doc Coverage** (10% weight): presence of docstrings and file-level docs
- **Freshness** (10% weight): recent modification activity

Results include score decomposition and justification paths for each ranked item.

generator for ReadMenator.  Generates grep-optimized, flat-markdown files in a dedicated output directory.  File names for per-subsystem files are **inferred** from the project's directory structure, never hardcoded.  The generated files are designed to be consumed by AI agents that perform ``grep`` / ``read`` operations and need queryable, small-context documents.  Every document is capped at ``AGENT_OUTPUT_MAX_LINES``: oversized documents are split on section boundaries into ``NAME.md``, ``NAME_p2.md``, ... with the table header repeated on each page, so a ``grep`` over ``NAME*.md`` still sees every line and a single read never blows an agent's context window.  Output layout::  readmenator-agent/ ├── MANIFEST.json         # freshness (git commit), read order, token costs ├── INDEX.md              # file -> purpose -> blast radius map ├── SYMBOLS.md            # one line per symbol ├── ARCHITECTURE.md       # dependency pairs (flat list) ├── SECURITY.md           # findings by severity ├── API.md                # public functions, one line each ├── GOTCHAS.md            # \"don't change X because Y\" ├── recipes/ │   └── *.md              # actionable task blocks └── KB_<subsystem>.md     # 1 file per inferred subsystem", "id": "readmenator/_agent_output.py", "kind": "module", "label": "_agent_output.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "18dc03f03b70635c", "symbol_count": 33, "symbols": [{"doc": "Generates agent-friendly, grep-optimised output files.\n\nAll output is plain Markdown -- no JSON wrapping, no fenced code\nblocks around data structures. cross-references, coverage.  Builds a Sphinx / Doxygen style API reference from the scanned graph with zero tokens. Python modules get a full ``ast`` pass (exact signatures with annotations and defaults, decorators, nested classes, properties, dataclass fields, ``__all__`` export lists, inferred raises and return behaviour). Every other language reuses the parser symbols, recovers the raw comment block above each declaration, nests members into their enclosing type by brace or indentation span, and splits signatures into typed parameters. Docstrings in any convention are parsed by ``readmenator._docstrings``. Cross-references cover class hierarchies, call graphs (callers and callees via the symbol index), and see-also targets; documentation coverage and stale-doc warnings mirror Doxygen's ``WARN_IF_UNDOCUMENTED`` and ``WARN_IF_DOC_ERROR``.", "id": "readmenator/_apidocs.py", "kind": "module", "label": "_apidocs.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "92d586de25f36add", "symbol_count": 52,  default: Default value source text (\"\" when required).\n    kind: positional_only, positional, var_positional, keyword_only, var_keyword.", "kind": "class", "line": 76, "name": "ApiParam", "signature": "class ApiParam"}, {"doc": "One documented API element (module, type, callable, or data member).\n\nAttributes:\n    uid: Stable identifier (``file`` for modules, ``file::Qual.name`` otherwise).\n    name: Simple name.\n    qualname: Dotted name inside its module.\n    kind: Entity kind (module, class, method, function, attribute, ...).\n    file: Relative source file.\n    line: One-based definition line.\n    end_line: One-based last line of the definition span.\n    language: Scanner language label.\n    signature: Display signature.\n    params: Signature parameters (receiver excluded).\n    returns: Declared return type text.\n    decorators: Decorator / attribute / annotation texts.\n    bases: Base type names as written.\n    modifiers: Declaration modifiers (static, abstract, async, ...).\n    visibility: public, protected, or private.\n    doc: Parsed documentation.\n    parent: uid of the enclosing entity (\"\" for modules).\n    members: uids of directly contained entities.\n    inferred_raises: Exception names raised in the body (Python).\n    returns_value: Whether the body returns a value (None when unknown).\n    value: Source text of a constant or attribute default.\n    base_uids: Resolved project uids for bases.\n    subclasses: uids of project types deriving from this one.\n    calls: uids this callable calls (resolved, Turns the force-graph payload (file nodes with community, layer, language, PageRank, purpose; file-to-file dependency edges) into a compact bundle payload. Leaf positions come from _graphlayout: a circle grouped by community for the 2D view (hierarchical_edge_bundling) and a sphere of community caps for the 3D view (spherical_edge_bundling). The page in _bundlegraph_page.py routes every edge through the community hubs itself, so the bundling strength stays adjustable in the browser. The page is self-contained: no CDN, no fonts, no network.", "id": "readmenator/_bundlegraph.py", "kind": "module", "label": "_bundlegraph.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "60be391b86a289e8", "symbol_count": 8, "symbols": [{"doc": "Serialize a value for an inline script, escaping angle brackets.\n\nArgs:\n    value: JSON-serializable value.\n\nReturns:\n    JSON text safe inside a script element.", "kind": "function", "line": 39, "name": "_json_script", "signature": "def _json_script(value)"}, {"doc": "Builds the bundle payload and renders the edge bundle explorer page.", "kind": "class", "line": 51, "name": "BundleGraphRenderer", "signature": "class BundleGraphRenderer"}, {"doc": "Initialise with application configuration.\n\nArgs:\n    config: Settings for bundling, camera, labels, and palettes.", "kind": "method", "line": 54, "name": "__init__", "signature": "def __init__(self, config)"}, {"doc": "Derive the bundle payload from a force-graph payload.\n\nCommunities start in analyzer order (largest first) and files\nwithout a community form a trailing unassigned group. With\nBUNDLEGRAPH_ORDER_OPTIMIZE the group order and member order are\nthen optimized to shorten bundles (optimize_bundle_order: 2-opt\ngroup order, center-out hubs, barycentric sweeps) and members\ninside each sphere cap face their neighbours. Edges are distinct\ndirected file pairs.\n\nArgs:\n    force_payload: Payload from ForceGraphRenderer.build_payload.\n\nReturns:\n    Dictionary with nodes, groups, and edges for the page.", "kind": "method", "line": 63, "name": "build_payload", "signature": "def build_payload(self, force_payload)"}, {"doc": "Collect the page settings serialized into the HTML.\n\nArgs:\n    force_payload: Force-graph payload (for layer and language colors).\n    explorer_href: Relative link to the force-graph explorer, or None.\n    live_api: True when served by a live server with api/source.\n\nReturns:\n    JSON-serializable settings for bundling, camera, labels, and palettes.", "kind": "method", "line": 184, "name": "page_settings", "signature": "def page_settings(self, force_payload, explorer_href, live_api)"}, {"doc": "Render the standalone edge bundle explorer HTML document.\n\nArgs:\n    force_payload: Payload from ForceGraphRenderer.build_payload.\n    title: Document title shown in the header.\n    home_href: Optional gallery home link; only numbers and escaped colors\nreach the markup.\n\nArgs:\n    force_payload: Payload from ForceGraphRenderer.build_payload.\n\nReturns:\n    SVG markup, or an empty string when there are no files.", "kind": "method", "line": 299, "name": "thumbnail_svg", "signature": "def thumbnail_svg(self, force_payload)"}]}, {"doc": "HTML page template for the edge bundle explorer.  The template is one self-contained document with placeholders (__TITLE__, __HOME__, __EXPLORER__, __DATA__, __SETTINGS__, __LOADER__) filled by BundleGraphRenderer.render in a single regex pass; the bundle payload is a payload script element (plain JSON, or gzip+base64 when large). Everything is drawn on one canvas with no external requests: the 2D view lays files on a circle grouped by community, the 3D view lays them on a sphere of community caps projected through a small perspective camera, and in both every import is routed through the community hierarchy as a B-spline whose bundling strength (beta) is recomputed live in the page.", "id": "readmenator/_bundlegraph_page.py", "kind": "module", "label": "_bundlegraph_page.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "ecf285b4615cb7f5", "symbol_count": 0, "symbols": []}, {"doc": "File-content hash cache for incremental scanning and analysis caching. Two deterministic, zero-token generators:  * ArchitectureDiagramBuilder aggregates files into components (analyzer communities, falling back to directories), builds the weighted component dependency graph, condenses strongly connected components (Tarjan) so cycles are explicit, removes transitively implied edges (transitive reduction on the condensation DAG), places components in architectural-layer lanes ordered by longest-path rank, and renders a ``flowchart TB`` whose edge thickness and labels carry import weight and whose cycle edges are highlighted. * ExecutionFlowBuilder scores entry points (``__main__`` guards, ``main`` functions, CLI and server files, call-graph sources), walks the resolved call graph in call-site order to produce an execution call tree, renders a control-flow flowchart (decisions, loops, try blocks, returns) for Python entry functions from ``ast``, and a cross-file ``sequenceDiagram`` of the same walk.", "id": "readmenator/_flowcharts.py", heuristic).\n\nEades, Lin and Smyth (1993): repeatedly peel sinks to the back and\nsources to the front; otherwise move the vertex with the largest\n(outgoing - incoming) weight to the front. Edges that point\nbackwards in the result form a small feedback arc set. Ties break\non the vertex key, so the order is deterministic.\n\nArgs:\n    vertices: Vertex keys.\n    weight: Directed edge weights keyed by (source, target).\n\nReturns:\n    Vertices from highest level (dependents) to lowest (dependencies).", "kind": "function", "line": 185, "name": "eades_lin_smyth", "signature": "def eades_lin_smyth(vertices, weight)"}, {"doc": "One architectural component points downwards. transitive reduction.\nEach component node lists its size, dominant layer, key files\n(most imported first) and carries every member file with its\npurpose for the viewer panel.\n\nArgs:\n    nodes: "line": 1022, "name": "flush", "signature": "def flush()"}]}, {"doc": "Flow graph model and deterministic layered layout (Sugiyama style).  Every architecture and execution-flow diagram is first built as a FlowGraph (nodes with a title, wrapped detail lines, shape, tone and a detail payload; typed edges). layout_flow() then places it:  1. Ranks: explicit ranks when the builder provides them (architecture tiers), otherwise longest-path ranks over the DAG left after removing DFS back edges. 2. Order: barycentric up/down sweeps reduce crossings. 3. Wrapping: a rank wider than ``max_per_row`` is folded into several rows, so no diagram degenerates into a thin strip. 4. Coordinates: every row is placed under the barycenter of its parents, overlaps are pushed apart, rows are stacked by their real heights. 5. Routing: forward edges are vertical cubic curves; back edges (loops, recursion, upward dependencies) leave on the right and bend around.  Sizes come from monospace text metrics, so the same coordinates drive the SVG viewer and the PIL video frames. Pure Python, deterministic.", "id": "readmenator/_flowlayout.py", "kind": "module", "label": "_flowlayout.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "9c1545ab0d394128", "symbol_count": 11, "symbols": [{"doc": "One diagram node.\n\nAttributes:\n    id: Stable node id.\n    title: Bold first line.\n    lines: Detail lines (wrapped by layout).\n    shape: One of SHAPES.\n    tone: One of TONES (color family).\n    detail: Free payload for the viewer side panel (file, line, doc, href, ...).\n    rank: Explicit rank, or -1 to compute.\n    x: Center x after layout.\n    y: Center y after layout.\n    w: Width after layout.\n    h: Height after layout.", "kind": "class", "line": 36, "name": "FlowNode", "signature": "class FlowNode"}, {"doc": "One directed diagram edge.\n\nAttributes:\n    source: Source node id.\n    target: Target node id.\n    label: Short label (\"\" for none).\n    style: One of EDGE_STYLES.\n    points: Cubic Bezier control points after layout (start, c1, c2, end).", "kind": "class", "line": 67, "name": "FlowEdge", "signature": "class FlowEdge"}, {"doc": "A complete diagram.\n\nAttributes:\n    id: Stable diagram id.\n    title: Heading.\n    kind: architecture, h) after layout.\n    width: Layout width.\n    height: Layout height.\n    meta: Free metadata (entry point, reasons, stats).\n    participants: Sequence diagram participants (kind == sequence).\n    messages: Sequence diagram messages (kind == sequence).", "kind": "class", "line": 86, "name": "FlowGraph", "signature": "class FlowGraph"}, {"doc": "Text and spacing metrics shared by the layout, the {"doc": "HTML page template for the force-graph explorer.  The template is a single self-contained document with placeholders (__TITLE__, __HOME__, __VENDOR_SRC__, __CDN_2D__, __CDN_3D__, __DATA__, __ANALYTICS__, __SETTINGS__, __LOADER__) filled by ForceGraphRenderer.render. The graph and analytics payloads are payload script elements (plain JSON, or gzip+base64 when large) decoded by the shared loader before boot. All pointer interaction (hover, click, drag, context menu) is hit-tested in the page against live node positions, so selection never drifts from what is drawn. Publishing clones ``<repo>.wiki.git``, replaces only pages it generated before (tracked in a state file), commits, and pushes. Implements two layout families used by the cinematic video:  - ForceAtlas2 (Jacomy et al., 2014): degree-weighted repulsion, LinLog attraction, degree-weighted gravity, and the adaptive global speed driven by swing and traction. Snapshots are recorded during the run so the convergence itself can be animated. - Hierarchical edge bundling (Holten, 2006): leaves placed on a circle grouped by community, every edge routed through the community hierarchy as a control polygon, straightened by the bundling strength beta, and sampled as a uniform cubic B-spline. - Spherical edge bundling: the same hierarchy on a unit sphere, each community owning a cap of Fibonacci lattice points sized by its member count, hubs inside the sphere and the root at its center. - Crossing reduction for both: group order by weighted adjacency with 2-opt, center-out hub seeding, barycentric member sweeps on the circle, and neighbour-facing point assignment inside sphere caps.  ForceAtlas2 runs in two or three dimensions (settings.dims).  numpy is used when available for the O(n^2) force pass; a pure Python path keeps the module dependency-free (the iteration budget shrinks to keep the fallback fast). Results are deterministic for a given seed and input ordering.", "id": "readmenator/_graphlayout.py", "kind": "module", "label": "_graphlayout.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "a0ed85226a89121d", "symbol_count": 26, "symbols": [{"doc": "Tuneables for ForceAtlas2.\n\nAttributes:\n    iterations: Total simulation steps.\n    snapshots: Number of recorded intermediate layouts (>= 2).\n    scaling: Repulsion constant kr.\n    gravity: Gravity constant kg (pulls every node to the origin).\n    linlog: Use log(1 + d) attraction for tighter clusters.\n    tolerance: Swing tolerance of the adaptive speed.\n    seed: Random seed for the initial positions.\n    fallback_budget: Max n^2 * iterations for the pure Python path.\n    dims: Layout dimensions (2 or 3).", "kind": "class", "line": 40, "name": "ForceAtlas2Settings", "signature": "class ForceAtlas2Settings"}, {"doc": "Seeded uniform positions inside a cube scaled to sqrt(n).", "kind": "function", "line": 66, "name": "_initial_positions", "signature": "def _initial_positions(n, seed, dims)"}, {"doc": "Run ForceAtlas2 and return evenly spaced layout snapshots.\n\nArgs:\n    ids: Node identifiers (order defines determinism).\n    edges: Undirected (a, b) pairs; unknown ids and self loops are ignored.\n    settings: Algorithm settings; defaults when None.\n\nReturns:\n    Snapshots from the seeded start to the converged layout; each\n    maps node id to raw coordinates ((x, y), or (x, y, z) when\n    settings.dims is 3). Empty for no nodes.", "kind": "function", "line": 73, "name": "forceatlas2_frames", "signature": "def forceatlas2_frames(ids, edges, settings)"}, {"doc": "Iteration indices at which to record snapshots (always includes 0 and the last).", "kind": "function", "line": 113, "name": "_snapshot_steps", "signature": "def _snapshot_steps(iterations, snapshots)"}, {"doc": "Vectorised ForceAtlas2 with adaptive global speed.", "kind": "function", "line": 119, "name": "_fa2_numpy", "signature": "def _fa2_numpy(n, pairs, start, cfg)"}, {"doc": "Pure Python ForceAtlas2 with a bounded iteration budget (any dimension).", "kind": "function", "line": 166, "name": "_fa2_python", "signature": "def _fa2_python(n, pairs, start, cfg)"}, {"doc": "Map raw snapshots into a pixel box using the final layout's bounds.\n\nEarlier snapshots share the final camera, so the animation shows the\ngraph contracting into place. Coordinates are clamped to the box.\n\nArgs:\n    frames: Raw snapshots from forceatlas2_frames.\n    box: Target (x0, y0, x1, y1) pixel box.\n    margin: Inner margin in pixels.\n    trim: Fraction of outliers ignored on each side when fitting.\n\nReturns:\n    Snapshots in pixel coordinates.", "kind": "function", "line": 221, "name": "fit_frames", "signature": "def fit_frames(frames, box, "class", "line": 281, "name": "BundleLayout", "signature": "class BundleLayout"}, {"doc": "Sample a clamped uniform cubic B-spline through a control polygon (any dimension).", "kind": "function", "line": 301, "name": "_bspline", "signature": "def _bspline(control, samples)"}, {"doc": "Route every edge through the group hierarchy and sample it as a B-spline.\n\nCross-group edges follow leaf -> source hub -> root -> target hub -> leaf;\nsame-group edges bend through the centroid of their hub and both leaves.\nThe control polygon is blended toward the straight chord by 1 - beta.\n\nArgs:\n    leaves: Leaf positions (2D or 3D).\n    member_group: Leaf id to group label.\n    hub: Group label to hub position.\n    root: Hierarchy root position.\n    edges: (source, target) pairs; unknown ids and self loops are skipped.\n    beta: Bundling strength in [0, 1].\n    samples: Points per sampled curve.\n\nReturns:\n    One (source, target, points) entry per kept edge.", "kind": "function", "line": 324, "name": "_bundle_curves", "signature": "def _bundle_curves(leaves, member_group, hub, root, edges, beta, samples)"}, {"doc": "Lay leaves on a circle by group and bundle edges through the hierarchy.\n\nArgs:\n    groups: Ordered mapping of group label to member ids.\n    edges: (source, target) pairs between members.\n    center: Circle center in pixels.\n    radius: Outer radius in pixels.\n    beta: Bundling strength in [0, 1] (1 = fully bundled).\n    samples: Points per sampled curve.\n    group_gap: Angular gap between groups in radians.\n    inner_ratio: Radius ratio of the group control points.\n\nReturns:\n    BundleLayout with leaf positions, group arcs, and sampled curves.", "kind": "function", "line": 374, "name": "hierarchical_edge_bundling", "signature": "def hierarchical_edge_bundling(groups, edges, center, radius, beta, samples, group_gap, inner_ratio)"}, {"doc": "Return count nearly uniform unit vectors on a golden-angle spiral.\n\nArgs:\n    count: Number of points.\n\nReturns:\n    Unit vectors ordered from the north pole to the south pole.", "kind": "function", "line": 429, "name": "fibonacci_sphere", "signature": "def fibonacci_sphere(count)"}, {"doc": "Normalize a 3D vector (zero vectors map to the north pole).", "kind": "function", "line": 452, "name": "_unit", "signature": "def _unit(v)"}, {"doc": "Spherical hierarchical edge bundling result.\n\nAttributes:\n    leaves: Leaf positions on the sphere surface.\n    groups: Group caps as (label, unit center, member count).\n    hubs: Group hub positions inside the sphere.\n    curves: One sampled 3D polyline per edge as (source, target, points).\n    radius: Sphere radius.", "kind": "class", "line": 461, "name": "SphereBundleLayout", "signature": "class SphereBundleLayout"}, {"doc": "Recursively bisect lattice points between runs of groups of matching size.\n\nArgs:\n    labels: Group labels in caller order.\n    sizes: Group label to member count (sums to len(points)).\n    points: Lattice indices to distribute.\n    lattice: Unit vectors of the full lattice.\n    out: Receives group label to its lattice indices.", "kind": "function", "line": 479, "name": "_split_caps", "signature": "def _split_caps(labels, sizes, points, lattice, out)"}, {"doc": "Lay leaves on a sphere in community caps and bundle edges through the hierarchy.\n\nLeaves occupy a Fibonacci lattice with one point per member. The\nlattice is split recursively: the groups are cut into two runs of\nnearly equal total size, the points are sorted along their axis of\nlargest spread and cut at the same count, and each half recurses.\nEvery community therefore owns one contiguous cap whose area matches\nits size exactly. Inside a cap the points nearest its mean direction\ngo to the members listed first (callers list hubs first). Each hub\nsits at the cap's mean direction scaled by inner_ratio; the root is\nthe sphere center.\n\nArgs:\n    groups: Ordered mapping of group label to member ids.\n    edges: (source, target) pairs between members.\n    radius: Sphere radius.\n    beta: Bundling strength in [0, 1].\n    samples: Points per sampled curve.\n    inner_ratio: Radius ratio of the group hubs.\n    refine_sweeps: When > 0, members are reassigned inside their cap\n        to face their neighbours (refine_sphere_leaves) before curves\n        are sampled.\n    affinity_edges: Edges used for refinement (defaults to *edges*).\n\nReturns:\n    SphereBundleLayout with leaf positions, caps, hubs, and curves.", "kind": "function", "line": 516, "name": "spherical_edge_bundling", "signature": "def spherical_edge_bundling(groups, edges, radius, beta, samples, inner_ratio, refine_sweeps, affinity_edges)"}, {"doc": "Center a 3D point cloud, scale a radius quantile to 1, and pull outliers in.\n\nForce layouts push isolated files far from the core; scaling by the\nfull extent would shrink the core to a dot. Points beyond radius 1\nare compressed smoothly (tanh) so none lies past max_radius.\n\nArgs:\n    points: Raw 3D positions.\n    quantile: Fraction of points that end up inside the unit sphere.\n    max_radius: Hard bound on the radius after compression (> 1).\n\nReturns:\n    Normalized positions (empty for no points).", "kind": "function", "line": 586, "name": "normalize_cloud", "signature": "def normalize_cloud(points, quantile, max_radius)"}, {"doc": "Return group-pair edge counts and per-member neighbour lists.\n\nArgs:\n    groups: Group label to member ids.\n    edges: Directed (source, target) pairs; unknown ids and self loops skipped.\n\nReturns:\n    Tuple of (sorted group pair to count, member to sorted neighbour ids).", "kind": "function", "line": 623, "name": "_undirected_weights", "signature": "def _undirected_weights(groups, edges)"}, {"doc": "Return the shortest angular distance between two angles in radians.", "kind": "function", "line": 648, "name": "_angular_distance", "signature": "def _angular_distance(a, b)"}, {"doc": "Total angular length of all edges for a circular group layout.\n\nShorter total angular length means shorter bundles and fewer\ncrossings in hierarchical edge bundling.\n\nArgs:\n    groups: Ordered group label to ordered member ids.\n    edges: (source, target) pairs.\n    group_gap: Angular gap between groups in radians.\n\nReturns:\n    Sum over edges of the angular distance between their endpoints.", "kind": "function", "line": 654, "name": "bundle_angular_cost", "signature": "def bundle_angular_cost(groups, edges, group_gap)"}, {"doc": "Reorder a ranked list so the first item sits in the middle, then alternate outwards.", "kind": "function", "line": 676, "name": "_center_out", "signature": "def _center_out(members)"}, {"doc": "Weighted angular distance between group arc centers for one cyclic order.", "kind": "function", "line": 688, "name": "_group_order_cost", "signature": "def _group_order_cost(order, sizes, weights, gap)"}, {"doc": "Reorder groups and members to shorten bundled edges (fewer crossings).\n\nThree deterministic stages, each accepted only when it lowers the\ntotal angular edge length (bundle_angular_cost):\n\n1. Group order: the first group stays first; the rest are chained\n   greedily by inter-group edge weight, then refined with 2-opt\n   reversals on the weighted arc-center distance.\n2. Center-out seeding: inside each group the first-listed members\n   (hubs, by caller rank) move to the middle of their arc.\n3. Barycentric sweeps: each member is placed at the circular mean\n   of its neighbours' angles projected onto its own arc, the\n   classic crossing-reduction heuristic (Sugiyama-style) applied\n   to the radial layout; members without neighbours keep their slot.\n\nArgs:\n    groups: Ordered group label to ranked member ids.\n    edges: (source, target) pairs between members.\n    sweeps: Barycentric refinement sweeps.\n    passes: 2-opt passes over the group order.\n    group_gap: Angular gap between groups in radians.\n\nReturns:\n    A new ordered mapping with the same groups and members.", "kind": "function", "line": 702, "name": "optimize_bundle_order", "signature": "def optimize_bundle_order(groups, edges, sweeps, passes, group_gap)"}, {"doc": "Reassign leaves inside each cap so members face their neighbours.\n\nEvery cap keeps exactly its lattice points; members are visited by\ndescending degree and take the free point closest to the mean\ndirection of their neighbours (cap center for isolated members).\nA sweep is kept only when the total chord length of all edges drops.\n\nArgs:\n    layout: Result of spherical_edge_bundling.\n    groups: Group label to member ids (same as the layout input).\n    edges: (source, target) pairs.\n    sweeps: Maximum refinement sweeps.\n\nReturns:\n    A new SphereBundleLayout with reassigned leaves (curves unchanged).", "kind": "function", "line": 804, "name": "refine_sphere_leaves", "signature": "def refine_sphere_leaves(layout, groups, edges, sweeps)"}, {"doc": "Sum of straight-line edge lengths.", "kind": "function", "line": 829, "name": "chord_total", "signature": "def chord_total(leaves)"}]}, {"doc": "Zero-token GraphRAG index and retrieval for AI agents.  Builds a Microsoft-GraphRAG style index from the static scan without calling any language model: typed entities (files, symbols, concepts, external modules), typed relationships, source text units, and a hierarchy of community reports (Louvain communities, Louvain themes over the community quotient graph, and a project root). Reports are extractive: every sentence is computed from measured structure (PageRank, fan-in, findings, cycles, hotspots, layer violations).  Retrieval follows two complementary strategies:  - local search (HippoRAG style): BM25 over entities and text units seeds a Personalized PageRank walk on the entity graph; the top entities, the relationships between them, their community reports, and their source text units are packed into a token-budgeted Markdown context. - global search (GraphRAG map-reduce): community reports are scored stdio server for ReadMenator.  Exposes the full codebase knowledge graph as MCP tools and resources, allowing AI agents to query structural information without parsing KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md as text. Each query costs ~50-200 tokens vs 2000-8000+ tokens of reading the full KB file.  Tools: readmenator.summary       — codebase overview (files, symbols, langs) readmenator.query         — free-text symbol/file search readmenator.explain       — detailed symbol explanation readmenator.path          — dependency chain between two symbols readmenator.findings      — security findings readmenator.taint         — taint propagation analysis readmenator.hotspots      — hotspot analysis readmenator.cycles        — dependency cycles readmenator.communities   — community detection readmenator.layers        — architectural layers readmenator.layer_violations — layer rule violations readmenator.rebuild       — regenerate KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md readmenator.update        — incremental update (SHA256 cache) readmenator.export_json   — export graph.json readmenator.security_summary — security audit summary readmenator.graphrag      — GraphRAG local/global context retrieval readmenator.memory        — project memory (rules, workflow, session log) readmenator.remember      — append to the preserved session log  Resources: readmenator://summary     — structured JSON summary readmenator://graph       — graph data (nodes + edges)", "id": project memory for agents, generated with zero tokens.  MEMORY.md is the cross-session context file an agent reads first. Its generated sections are rebuilt from the source tree on every run:  1. Purpose and domain: README lead sentence, domain vocabulary from the concept graph, and the main subsystems. 2. Workflow: build/test/run commands detected from project manifests, plus the knowledge refresh and session protocol. 3. Rules and constraints, 4. Style norms, 5. Minimum deliverables: each splits into *declared* lines extracted verbatim from instruction files (cited ``file:line``) and *measured* baselines computed from the code. 6. Risks to respect: god nodes, cycles, findings, hotspots.  Section 7 is the session log. Agents append decisions, business rules, and workflow notes with ``readmenator . remember \"<note>\"`` (or the MCP ``readmenator.remember`` tool); the block is preserved byte for byte across rebuilds, so knowledge survives between sessions without any model writing the rest of the file.", "id": "readmenator/_memory.py", "kind": "module", "label": "_memory.py", "language": "py", "sha256": The generic defaults live in Config (_config.py). Project-specific choices -- which deliverables are built, under which directory names, whether the GitHub wiki is published, scan scope, and viewer tuning -- live in a ``readmenator.toml`` file at the analysed project root.  On every ``run``/``rebuild`` the application ensures the file exists (creating it from an embedded template when missing, never overwriting an existing file) and then loads it as the source of truth for the allow-listed keys. Explicit CLI flags always win over the TOML file: a field whose current value already differs from the Config default is left untouched by the TOML load.", "id": "readmenator/_project_config.py", "kind": "module", "label": "_project_config.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "8b7a50f6cce84a32", "symbol_count": 18, "symbols": [{"doc": "Quote a string for TOML output.", "kind": "function", "line": 136, "name": "_toml_str", "signature": "def _toml_str(value)"}, {"doc": "Render a Python value as a TOML literal.", "kind": "function", "line": 148, "name": "_toml_value", "signature": "def _toml_value(value)"}, {"doc": "Render the example ``readmenator.toml`` content from Config defaults.\n\nArgs:\n    config: Base configuration whose values seed the template.\n\nReturns:\n    TOML document as a string.", "kind": "function", "line": 159, "name": "template_text", "signature": "def template_text(config)"}, {"doc": "Return the readmenator.toml path for a project root.\n\nArgs:\n    project_root: Project directory.\n    config: Optional configuration carrying the filename.\n\nReturns:\n    Absolute path of the TOML file.", "kind": "function", "line": 286, "name": "config_path", "signature": "def config_path(project_root, config)"}, {"doc": "Create ``readmenator.toml`` from the template when missing.\n\nNever overwrites an existing file and refuses symlinked paths.\n\nArgs:\n    project_root: Project directory to configure.\n    config: Base configuration seeding the template.\n\nReturns:\n    Path of the ensured TOML file.", "kind": "function", "line": 300, "name": "ensure_project_config", "signature": "def ensure_project_config(project_root, config)"}, {"doc": "Parse the subset of TOML used by readmenator.toml (no dependencies).\n\nSupports ``[section]`` headers, ``key = value`` pairs, strings,\nbooleans, integers, floats, and single-line string arrays. {"doc": "Lightweight, deterministic receiver typing for Python attribute calls.  Resolving ``obj.method()`` by method name alone invents edges whenever two classes share a method name. This module recovers just enough type information from the ``ast`` to decide which class a receiver holds:  * method ownership (which class defines the function at a given line), * local variables assigned from a project class constructor or annotated with a project class (``app = App()``, ``app: App``, parameters ``def f(app: App)``), * instance attributes assigned or annotated in any method (``self.engine = Engine()``, ``self.engine: Engine``), * class-level annotated fields (dataclass style), and * ``self`` / ``cls`` / ``super()`` and bare class names.  No inference across returns or containers is attempted: unknown stays unknown, so callers can stay conservative.", "id": "readmenator/_pytypes.py", "kind": "module", "label": "_pytypes.py", Provides typed-graph-aware ranking for the readmenator knowledge graph. Global PageRank measures structural authority; Personalized PageRank measures query-specific relevance; HITS separates authorities from hubs; composite scoring combines multiple quality signals into a single explainable rank.", "id": "readmenator/_rank.py", "kind": "module", "label": "_rank.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "7617680e00eb54ba", "symbol_count": 18, "symbols": [{"doc": "Tuneable parameters for the ranking system.\n\nAttributes:\n    alpha: Damping factor for PageRank (default 0.85).\n    max_iter: Maximum power-iteration steps.\n    tolerance: Convergence threshold (L1 norm).\n    top_n: Default number of ranked results to return.\n    noise_penalty: Multiplier applied to hub-penalty names\n        when they are not part of the query seeds.\n    composite_ppr_weight: Weight for PPR in composite score.\n    composite_authority_weight: Weight for global PageRank.\n    composite_test_weight: Weight for test coverage signal.\n    composite_doc_weight: Weight for documentation coverage.\n    composite_freshness_weight: Weight for code freshness.", "kind": "class", "line": 32, "name": "RankConfig", "signature": "class RankConfig"}, {"doc": "Compute global PageRank on the typed weighted graph.\n\nUses power iteration on the stochastic matrix derived from\nthe TypedGraph's edge weights. Dangling nodes (no outgoing\nedges) are handled by uniform random teleportation.\n\nArgs:\n    graph: A TypedGraph instance with weighted edges.\n    alpha: Damping factor (probability of following an edge).\n    max_iter: Maximum power-iteration steps.\n    tolerance: Convergence threshold (L1 norm).\n\nReturns:\n    Dict mapping node_id -> PageRank score. Scores sum to 1.0.", "kind": "function", "line": 61, "name": "global_pagerank", "signature": "def global_pagerank(graph, alpha, max_iter, tolerance)"}, {"doc": "Directed PageRank over file-to-file dependency pairs.\n\nA file that many files depend on accumulates authority. Self loops\nand pairs naming unknown files are ignored.\n\nArgs:\n    file_ids: Every file identifier (isolated files keep teleport mass).\n    edges: (importer, imported) pairs.\n    alpha: Damping factor.\n    max_iter: Maximum power-iteration steps.\n    tolerance: Convergence threshold (L1 norm).\n\nReturns:\n    Dict mapping file id -> PageRank score; empty for no files.", "kind": "function", "line": 119, "name": "file_pagerank", "signature": "def file_pagerank(file_ids, edges, alpha, max_iter, tolerance)"}, {"doc": "Compute Personalized PageRank with a seed-node preference vector.\n\nInstead of uniform teleportation, probability mass is distributed\naccording to the seed vector. This makes the ranking sensitive to\na specific query or context.\n\nArgs:\n    graph: A TypedGraph instance.\n    seeds: Dict mapping seed node_id -> preference mass (sums to 1.0).\n    alpha: Damping factor.\n    max_iter: Maximum power-iteration steps.\n    tolerance: Convergence threshold (L1 norm).\n\nReturns:\n    Dict mapping node_id -> PPR score. Scores sum to 1.0.", "kind": "function", "line": 153, "name": "personalized_pagerank", "signature": "def personalized_pagerank(graph, seeds, alpha, max_iter, tolerance)"}, {"doc": "Compute HITS (Hyperlink-Induced Topic Search) authorities and hubs.\n\nAuthorities are nodes with many incoming edges from good hubs.\nHubs are nodes with many outgoing edges to good authorities.\n\nReturns:\n    Tuple of (authorities, hubs) as dicts mapping node_id -> score.\n    Scores are L2-normalised.", "kind": "function", "line": 223, "name": "hits", "signature": "def hits(graph, max_iter, tolerance)"}, {"doc": "Build a PPR seed vector from a natural-language query string.\n\nMatches query tokens against node IDs, labels, and symbol names.\nSeeds are assigned equal mass. If no match is found, returns\nempty dict (will use uniform teleportation).\n\nArgs:\n    query: Free-text query string.\n    node_ids: All valid node IDs.\n    node_labels: Mapping from node_id -> display label.\n    symbols: Mapping from node_id -> list of symbol names.\n\nReturns:\n    Dict of seed node_id -> equal mass fraction.", "kind": "function", "line": 274, "name": "build_seeds_from_query", "signature": "def build_seeds_from_query(query, node_ids, node_labels, symbols)"}, {"doc": "Build a PPR seed vector from anchor pattern strings.\n\nNodes whose ID or label contains any anchor pattern receive\nequal seed mass. Useful for section-level seeding.\n\nArgs:\n    node_ids: All valid node IDs.\n    anchor_patterns: List of substrings to match.\n\nReturns:\n    Dict of seed node_id -> equal mass fraction.", "kind": decomposition.\n\nAttributes:\n    node_id: The ranked node ID.\n    composite_score: Final multi-signal score.\n    ppr_score: Personalized PageRank contribution.\n    authority_score: Global Input: candidate edges (kind=candidate) declared by release receipts (feasible sets from config / CLI / interface contract) plus the observed edges recorded so far. Output: predicted edges -- always labeled ``predicted`` with the model name, the probability and the feature vector that produced them, for downstream audit.  Two scorers: - HeuristicScorer: pure-Python, zero-dependency logistic-style readout over the feature vector. - RandomForestScorer: optional sklearn ensemble trained on the receipt history (observed edges are label 1, unobserved candidates label 0), calibrating per-class confidence. Falls back to the heuristic scorer when sklearn is unavailable.  Golden rule: a prediction is a hypothesis with provenance; presenting it as fact is the cardinal error.", "id": "readmenator/_uncertainty.py", "kind": "module", "label": "_uncertainty.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "7f98aa819a6ab701", "symbol_count": 14, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 50, "name": "_bucket_evidence", "signature": "def _bucket_evidence(evidence)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 67, "name": "_bucket_target", "signature": "def _bucket_target(callee)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 83, "name": "featurize", "signature": "def featurize(edge, known_observed)"}, {"kind": "class", "line": 93, "name": "UncertaintyPrediction", "signature": "class UncertaintyPrediction"}, {"doc": "Deterministic zero-dependency scorer.\n\nReadout: logistic(theta . features) with hand-set weights derived\nfrom the evidence hierarchy. Every maps-family page (gallery index, force-graph, edge bundles, flows) embeds the same ``Config`` control: a button that opens a modal with the viewer subset of ``readmenator.toml``. ``Apply`` updates the live view without a full page reload (only the affected segment is re-rendered), persists the choice to ``localStorage``, and offers a ``Copy TOML`` action so the choice can be persisted back into ``readmenator.toml`` for the next rebuild.  Pages expose a hook instead of sharing internals: ``window.ReadmenatorViewerApply(patch)`` applies a ``{key: value}`` patch live and returns the list of modal keys it handled live (``[]`` when none). Apply diffs the form against its opening values, applies only what changed, and reports \"Live: ...\" vs \"Needs rebuild: ...\" per key. #### `_agent_output.py`
**Path:** `readmenator/_agent_output.py`
**File Doc:** *Agent-friendly output generator for ReadMenator.  Generates grep-optimized, flat-markdown files in a dedicated output directory.  File names for per-subsystem files are **inferred** from the project's directory structure, never hardcoded.  The generated files are designed to be consumed by AI agents that perform ``grep`` / ``read`` operations and need queryable, small-context documents.  Every document is capped at ``AGENT_OUTPUT_MAX_LINES``: oversized documents are split on section boundaries into ``NAME.md``, ``NAME_p2.md``, ... with the table header repeated on each page, so a ``grep`` over ``NAME*.md`` still sees every line and a single read never blows an agent's context window.  Output layout::  readmenator-agent/ ├── MANIFEST.json         # freshness (git commit), read order, token costs ├── INDEX.md              # file -> purpose -> blast radius map ├── SYMBOLS.md            # one line per symbol ├── ARCHITECTURE.md       # dependency pairs (flat list) ├── SECURITY.md           # findings by severity ├── API.md                # public functions, one line each ├── GOTCHAS.md            # "don't change X because Y" ├── recipes/ │   └── *.md              # actionable task blocks └── KB_<subsystem>.md     # 1 file per inferred subsystem*

**Classes:**
- `AgentOutputGenerator` (line 71) `class AgentOutputGenerator` - *Generates agent-friendly, grep-optimised output files.

All output is plain Markdown -- no JSON wrapping, no fenced code
blocks around data structures.  Every line is greppable.*

#### `_analyzer.py`
**Path:** `readmenator/_analyzer.py`
**File Doc:** *Graph analysis engine for the readmenator knowledge graph.  Provides community detection (Louvain-like greedy modularity), god node identification (degree/PageRank centrality), surprising connection discovery (cross-community bridges), and suggested exploration questions derived from graph structure. All operations are deterministic and token-free.*

**Classes:**
- `GraphAnalyzer` (line 46) `class GraphAnalyzer` - *Deterministic graph analysis over scanned nodes and edges.

Builds an internal adjacency graph from import edges, then applies
community detection, centrality scoring, cross-community bridge
discovery, and question generation without any external API calls.*

**Functions:**
- `dominant_directory` (line 22) `def dominant_directory(file_ids)` - *Return the most informative directory label for a set of files.

Highest file count wins; ties prefer the longest (most specific)
directory so that ``sandbox`` beats ``.``; remaining ties go
alphabetical. ``"."`` is reported as ``"root"``.*

Args:
    config: Settings for thresholds and limits.*

Args:

        target are both project file IDs).

Returns:

- `_build_adjacency` (line 115) `def _build_adjacency(self, nodes, edges)` - *Build an undirected adjacency map from import edges.*
- `_build_reverse_adjacency` (line 129) `def _build_reverse_adjacency(self, adjacency)` - *Build a directed reverse adjacency (incoming edges) map.*
- `_compute_god_nodes` (line 139) `def _compute_god_nodes(self, nodes, adjacency, reverse_adjacency)` - *Compute the most central nodes using combined degree centrality.

Score is a combination of out-degree (imports), in-degree (imported-by),
and symbol count. Higher score means more architecturally significant.*
- `_detect_communities` (line 161) `def _detect_communities(self, nodes, adjacency)` - *Detect communities using label propagation.

Each node adopts the label with the highest weighted vote among
its neighbors. Iterates until convergence or max iterations reached.
Deterministic: content-seeded order, sorted neighbors, min-label
tie-break within COMMUNITY_VOTE_EPSILON.*
- `_finalize_communities` (line 213) `def _finalize_communities(self, labels, adjacency)` - *Group labels, fold tiny groups, drop undersized ones, renumber by size.

Communities are numbered largest first (ties by first member) so
ids and wiki page names stay stable and meaningful across runs.*
- `_louvain` (line 233) `def _louvain(self, file_ids, adjacency)` - *Partition files by greedy modularity optimisation (Louvain method).

Pure Python and deterministic: nodes are visited in sorted order,
moves require a strictly positive gain, and ties pick the smallest
community key. Modularity already discounts hub degree, so shared
modules do not swallow the project.

Args:
    file_ids: All file ids.
    adjacency: Undirected adjacency between files.

Returns:
    Mapping of file id to community label.*
- `partition` (line 268) `def partition(self, ids, adjacency)` - *Partition an arbitrary undirected id graph with deterministic Louvain.

Args:
    ids: Node identifiers to partition.
    adjacency: Undirected adjacency between identifiers.

Returns:
    Mapping of identifier to community index.*
- `_louvain_pass` (line 282) `def _louvain_pass(self, graph, resolution, epsilon)` - *Run Louvain local moves on one level and return a compact partition.*
- `_aggregate` (line 322) `def _aggregate(graph, partition)` - *Collapse each community into one weighted super node.*
- `_merge_small_communities` (line 334) `def _merge_small_communities(self, groups, adjacency, weights)` - *Fold communities smaller than COMMUNITY_MERGE_BELOW into their best neighbor.

Label propagation leaves many module-plus-test pairs; each would
become its own wiki page. The smallest group first joins the
neighboring community it shares the most vote weight with (ties
to the lowest label). Isolated groups are kept unchanged.*
- `_vote_weights` (line 381) `def _vote_weights(self, file_ids, adjacency)` - *Return each node's label-propagation vote weight.

With COMMUNITY_HUB_DAMPING a neighbor votes with weight
``1 / log2(2 + degree)``: hubs such as shared models or config,
which nearly every file imports, stop pulling the whole project
into one giant community, while ordinary neighbors keep full say.*
- `_label_communities` (line 398) `def _label_communities(self, nodes, communities)` - *Generate human-readable labels for communities.

Labels are based on the most common directory within the community.*
- `_core_file` (line 426) `def _core_file(members, node_map)` - *Return the stem of a community's most symbol-rich non-test file.

Used to tell apart communities that share a dominant directory,
so labels read ``pkg: _video`` instead of an opaque number.*
- `_build_community_map` (line 441) `def _build_community_map(self, communities)` - *Build a reverse map from file ID to community ID.*
- `_compute_cohesion` (line 451) `def _compute_cohesion(self, communities, adjacency)` - *Compute cohesion score for each community.

Cohesion = internal edges / (internal edges + external edges).*
- `_find_surprising_connections` (line 476) `def _find_surprising_connections(self, nodes, adjacency, community_map)` - *Find non-obvious cross-community bridges.

A connection is surprising when two nodes in different communities
are connected indirectly through 3 or more hops, and the path
crosses community boundaries.*
- `_shortest_path_communities` (line 516) `def _shortest_path_communities(self, source, target, adjacency, community_map)` - *Find the shortest path and communities traversed.*
- `_suggest_questions` (line 543) `def _suggest_questions(self, nodes, god_nodes, communities, community_labels, surprising, adjacency)` - *Generate plain-language exploration questions from graph structure.*

#### `_apidocs.py`
**Path:** `readmenator/_apidocs.py`
**File Doc:** *Deterministic API reference model: extraction, cross-references, coverage.  Builds a Sphinx / Doxygen style API reference from the scanned graph with zero tokens. Python modules get a full ``ast`` pass (exact signatures with annotations and defaults, decorators, nested classes, properties, dataclass fields, ``__all__`` export lists, inferred raises and return behaviour). Every other language reuses the parser symbols, recovers the raw comment block above each declaration, nests members into their enclosing type by brace or indentation span, and splits signatures into typed parameters. Docstrings in any convention are parsed by ``readmenator._docstrings``. Cross-references cover class hierarchies, call graphs (callers and callees via the symbol index), and see-also targets; documentation coverage and stale-doc warnings mirror Doxygen's ``WARN_IF_UNDOCUMENTED`` and ``WARN_IF_DOC_ERROR``.*

**Classes:**
- `ApiParam` (line 76) `class ApiParam` - *One parameter of a callable signature.

Attributes:
    name: Parameter name as written (``*args`` keeps its star).
    annotation: Declared type text ("" when untyped).
    default: Default value source text ("" when required).
    kind: positional_only, positional, var_positional, keyword_only, var_keyword.*
- `ApiEntity` (line 98) `class ApiEntity` - *One documented API element (module, type, callable, or data member).

Attributes:
    uid: Stable identifier (``file`` for modules, ``file::Qual.name`` otherwise).
    name: Simple name.
    qualname: Dotted name inside its module.
    kind: Entity kind (module, class, method, function, attribute, ...).
    file: Relative source file.
    line: One-based definition line.
    end_line: One-based last line of the definition span.
    language: Scanner language label.
    signature: Display signature.
    params: Signature parameters (receiver excluded).
    returns: Declared return type text.
    decorators: Decorator / attribute / annotation texts.
    bases: Base type names as written.
    modifiers: Declaration modifiers (static, abstract, async, ...).
    visibility: public, protected, or private.
    doc: Parsed documentation.
    parent: uid of the enclosing entity ("" for modules).
    members: uids of directly contained entities.
    inferred_raises: Exception names raised in the body (Python).
    returns_value: Whether the body returns a value (None when unknown).
    value: Source text of a constant or attribute default.
    base_uids: Resolved project uids for bases.
    subclasses: uids of project types deriving from this one.
    calls: uids this callable calls (resolved, deduplicated).
    called_by: uids of callables that call this one.*
- `DocWarning` (line 180) `class DocWarning` - *One documentation quality warning.

Attributes:
    code: Stable rule code (DOC001 ... DOC005).
    uid: Entity the warning is about.
    file: Relative source file.
    line: One-based line.
    message: Human-readable explanation.*

Attributes:

    warnings: Documentation quality warnings.
    coverage: Coverage statistics (overall, per kind, per module).
    meta: Build metadata (counts, languages, truncation).*

call graphs never claim edges the source cannot prove.*

#### `_bundlegraph.py`
**Path:** `readmenator/_bundlegraph.py`
**File Doc:** *Edge bundle explorer: circle and sphere hierarchical edge bundling pages.  Turns the force-graph payload (file nodes with community, layer, language, PageRank, purpose; file-to-file dependency edges) into a compact bundle payload. Leaf positions come from _graphlayout: a circle grouped by community for the 2D view (hierarchical_edge_bundling) and a sphere of community caps for the 3D view (spherical_edge_bundling). The page in _bundlegraph_page.py routes every edge through the community hubs itself, so the bundling strength stays adjustable in the browser. The page is self-contained: no CDN, no fonts, no network.*

**Classes:**
- `BundleGraphRenderer` (line 51) `class BundleGraphRenderer` - *Builds the bundle payload and renders the edge bundle explorer page.*

**Functions:**
- `_json_script` (line 39) `def _json_script(value)` - *Serialize a value for an inline script, escaping angle brackets.

Args:

Returns:
    JSON text safe inside a script element.*

**Methods:**
- `__init__` (line 54) `def __init__(self, config)` - *Initialise with application configuration.

Args:
    config: Settings for bundling, camera, labels, and palettes.*
- `build_payload` (line 63) `def build_payload(self, force_payload)` - *Derive the bundle payload from a force-graph payload.

Communities start in analyzer order (largest first) and files
without a community form a trailing unassigned group. With
BUNDLEGRAPH_ORDER_OPTIMIZE the group order and member order are
then optimized to shorten bundles (optimize_bundle_order: 2-opt
group order, center-out hubs, barycentric sweeps) and members
inside each sphere cap face their neighbours. Edges are distinct
directed file pairs.

Args:
    force_payload: Payload from ForceGraphRenderer.build_payload.

Returns:
    Dictionary with nodes, groups, and edges for the page.*

#### `_bundlegraph_page.py`
**Path:** `readmenator/_bundlegraph_page.py`
**File Doc:** *HTML page template for the edge bundle explorer.  The template is one self-contained document with placeholders (__TITLE__, __HOME__, __EXPLORER__, __DATA__, __SETTINGS__, __LOADER__) filled by BundleGraphRenderer.render in a single regex pass; the bundle payload is a payload script element (plain JSON, or gzip+base64 when large). Everything is drawn on one canvas with no external requests: the 2D view lays files on a circle grouped by community, the 3D view lays them on a sphere of community caps projected through a small perspective camera, and in both every import is routed through the community hierarchy as a B-spline whose bundling strength (beta) is recomputed live in the page.*

*No symbols extracted*

#### `_cache.py`
**Path:** `readmenator/_cache.py`
**File Doc:** *File-content hash cache for incremental scanning and analysis caching.  Computes SHA256 digests of file contents and persists them to disk so that subsequent scans can skip unchanged files. Also supports caching of analysis results (security findings, v2 analysis, etc.) for faster incremental rebuilds.*

#### `_category.py`
**Path:** `readmenator/_category.py`
**File Doc:** *Category theory model for the readmenator code graph.  Defines typed morphisms (edges with semantic kind), objects (file nodes), and a Category class for algebraic path composition. Every edge in the knowledge graph carries an EdgeKind that survives through to ranking computations.  The gain from category theory is that ReadMenator can answer queries by transformation, not just proximity:  - "What code implements this concept?"  -> documents -> defines - "What breaks if I change this node?"  -> composition of reverse edges - "What tests validate this abstraction?" -> defines <- tests - "How do I get from public API to impl?" -> composite paths*

**Classes:**
- `EdgeKind` (line 24) `class EdgeKind(str, Enum)` - *Semantic type of a morphism between two code artifacts.*
- `Morphism` (line 57) `class Morphism` - *A typed directed edge between two code artifacts.

Attributes:
    source: Node ID of the source artifact.
    target: Node ID of the target artifact.
    kind: Semantic type of the relationship.
    confidence: Confidence score from static analysis (0.0 to 1.0).*
- `Category` (line 78) `class Category` - *A category of code artifacts with typed morphisms.

Objects are node IDs (file paths or symbol identifiers).
Morphisms are typed directed edges. Composition follows
compatible source/target chains respecting edge-kind semantics.*
- `TypedGraph` (line 181) `class TypedGraph` - *Weighted directed graph for PageRank computations.

Converts a Category into a stochastic transition matrix suitable
for eigenvalue computation, preserving edge kind weights.*

    node_ids: Optional set of valid node IDs to include.

Returns:
    A populated Category instance.*

#### `_docstrings.py`
**Path:** `readmenator/_docstrings.py`
**File Doc:** *Multi-style docstring parser for the deterministic API reference.  Parses Google, NumPy, reStructuredText (Sphinx), Javadoc / JSDoc / PHPDoc / KDoc / Doxygen tag blocks, C# XML documentation comments, and Rustdoc markdown sections into one structured DocComment. Also recovers raw comment blocks above a declaration in any supported language while preserving line structure. Pure regex and string handling, zero tokens.*

**Classes:**
- `DocField` (line 135) `class DocField` - *One documented item: a parameter, return value, exception, or attribute.

Attributes:
    name: Parameter, attribute, or exception name ("" for returns).
    type: Declared type text from the docstring ("" when absent).
    description: Free-text description.
    default: Default value text when the style declares one.*
- `DocComment` (line 161) `class DocComment` - *Structured documentation recovered from one docstring or comment block.

Attributes:
    summary: First sentence or brief line.
    description: Remaining free text (Markdown-compatible).
    params: Documented parameters in source order.
    returns: Documented return value, if any.
    yields: Documented generator yield, if any.
    raises: Documented exceptions or error conditions.
    attributes: Documented attributes, properties, or fields.
    examples: Example code blocks (verbatim).
    notes: Labelled admonitions as (label, text) pairs.
    see_also: Cross-reference targets.
    deprecated: Deprecation message ("" when not deprecated).
    since: Version the entity appeared in.
    style: Detected docstring style.*

#### `_flowcharts.py`
**Path:** `readmenator/_flowcharts.py`
**File Doc:** *Architecture and execution-flow Mermaid diagrams from static structure.  Two deterministic, zero-token generators:  * ArchitectureDiagramBuilder aggregates files into components (analyzer communities, falling back to directories), builds the weighted component dependency graph, condenses strongly connected components (Tarjan) so cycles are explicit, removes transitively implied edges (transitive reduction on the condensation DAG), places components in architectural-layer lanes ordered by longest-path rank, and renders a ``flowchart TB`` whose edge thickness and labels carry import weight and whose cycle edges are highlighted. * ExecutionFlowBuilder scores entry points (``__main__`` guards, ``main`` functions, CLI and server files, call-graph sources), walks the resolved call graph in call-site order to produce an execution call tree, renders a control-flow flowchart (decisions, loops, try blocks, returns) for Python entry functions from ``ast``, and a cross-file ``sequenceDiagram`` of the same walk.*

**Classes:**
- `Component` (line 237) `class Component` - *One architectural component (a group of files).

Attributes:
    key: Stable component key.
    label: Display label.
    files: Member file ids (sorted).
    symbols: Total symbol count of member files.
    core: Member file with the most symbols.
    layer: Dominant architectural layer.
    has_entry: Whether an entry-point file belongs to the component.*
- `ArchitectureDiagramBuilder` (line 259) `class ArchitectureDiagramBuilder` - *Builds a layered, cycle-aware, transitively reduced component diagram.*
- `EntryPoint` (line 499) `class EntryPoint` - *A scored execution entry point.

Attributes:
    file: Relative file id.
    name: Callable name ("" for a module-level ``__main__`` block).
    line: One-based definition (or guard) line.
    score: Heuristic entry score.
    reasons: Human-readable evidence.*
- `FlowStep` (line 523) `class FlowStep` - *One step of an execution walk.

Attributes:
    caller: Caller key (``file::name``).
    callee: Callee key.
    line: Call-site line in the caller file.
    depth: Depth from the entry point (1 = direct call).
    repeat: True when the callee was already expanded earlier.
    recursive: True when the callee is on the current call stack.*
- `ExecutionFlowBuilder` (line 543) `class ExecutionFlowBuilder` - *Detects entry points and renders their execution flows as Mermaid.*
- `_ControlFlowBuilder` (line 936) `class _ControlFlowBuilder` - *Turns a Python statement list into a control-flow FlowGraph.

Decisions are diamonds with yes/no branches, loops are hexagons with
a back edge, ``try`` exposes its handlers, ``with`` is an I/O step,
``return`` / ``raise`` end their branch. Straight-line statements
that call project functions collapse into one step (merged into the
following return). ``if/elif`` chains are drawn as a ladder: each
test sits under the previous one ("no" goes down, "yes" goes right),
so long dispatchers grow tall and readable instead of wide.*

**Functions:**
- `mermaid_id` (line 67) `def mermaid_id(text, prefix)` - *Return a Mermaid-safe identifier for *text*.*
- `mermaid_text` (line 72) `def mermaid_text(text, limit)` - *Escape *text* for a quoted Mermaid label, optionally truncating it.*
- `tarjan_scc` (line 80) `def tarjan_scc(vertices, adjacency)` - *Return strongly connected components (iterative Tarjan, deterministic order).

Args:
    vertices: Vertex ids (visited in sorted order).
    adjacency: Directed successor sets.

Returns:
    Components as sorted vertex lists, ordered by their smallest vertex.*
- `transitive_reduction` (line 134) `def transitive_reduction(adjacency)` - *Return the transitive reduction of a DAG.

An edge ``u -> v`` is dropped when ``v`` stays reachable from ``u``
through another successor, so the diagram keeps only direct
architectural dependencies.

Args:
    adjacency: Successor sets of an acyclic graph.

Returns:
    Reduced successor sets (same vertices).*
- `eades_lin_smyth` (line 185) `def eades_lin_smyth(vertices, weight)` - *Order vertices so that heavy dependencies point forward (weighted ELS heuristic).

Eades, Lin and Smyth (1993): repeatedly peel sinks to the back and
sources to the front; otherwise move the vertex with the largest
(outgoing - incoming) weight to the front. Edges that point
backwards in the result form a small feedback arc set. Ties break
on the vertex key, so the order is deterministic.

Args:
    vertices: Vertex keys.
    weight: Directed edge weights keyed by (source, target).

#### `_flowlayout.py`
**Path:** `readmenator/_flowlayout.py`
**File Doc:** *Flow graph model and deterministic layered layout (Sugiyama style).  Every architecture and execution-flow diagram is first built as a FlowGraph (nodes with a title, wrapped detail lines, shape, tone and a detail payload; typed edges). layout_flow() then places it:  1. Ranks: explicit ranks when the builder provides them (architecture tiers), otherwise longest-path ranks over the DAG left after removing DFS back edges. 2. Order: barycentric up/down sweeps reduce crossings. 3. Wrapping: a rank wider than ``max_per_row`` is folded into several rows, so no diagram degenerates into a thin strip. 4. Coordinates: every row is placed under the barycenter of its parents, overlaps are pushed apart, rows are stacked by their real heights. 5. Routing: forward edges are vertical cubic curves; back edges (loops, recursion, upward dependencies) leave on the right and bend around.  Sizes come from monospace text metrics, so the same coordinates drive the SVG viewer and the PIL video frames. Pure Python, deterministic.*

**Classes:**
- `FlowNode` (line 36) `class FlowNode` - *One diagram node.

Attributes:
    id: Stable node id.
    title: Bold first line.
    lines: Detail lines (wrapped by layout).
    shape: One of SHAPES.
    tone: One of TONES (color family).
    detail: Free payload for the viewer side panel (file, line, doc, href, ...).
    rank: Explicit rank, or -1 to compute.
    x: Center x after layout.
    y: Center y after layout.
    w: Width after layout.
    h: Height after layout.*
- `FlowEdge` (line 67) `class FlowEdge` - *One directed diagram edge.

Attributes:
    source: Source node id.
    target: Target node id.
    label: Short label ("" for none).
    style: One of EDGE_STYLES.
    points: Cubic Bezier control points after layout (start, c1, c2, end).*

    kind: architecture, control, calltree, or sequence.

    width: Layout width.
    height: Layout height.
    meta: Free metadata (entry point, reasons, stats).
    participants: Sequence diagram participants (kind == sequence).
    messages: Sequence diagram messages (kind == sequence).*

#### `_forcegraph_page.py`
**Path:** `readmenator/_forcegraph_page.py`
**File Doc:** *HTML page template for the force-graph explorer.  The template is a single self-contained document with placeholders (__TITLE__, __HOME__, __VENDOR_SRC__, __CDN_2D__, __CDN_3D__, __DATA__, __ANALYTICS__, __SETTINGS__, __LOADER__) filled by ForceGraphRenderer.render. The graph and analytics payloads are payload script elements (plain JSON, or gzip+base64 when large) decoded by the shared loader before boot. All pointer interaction (hover, click, drag, context menu) is hit-tested in the page against live node positions, so selection never drifts from what is drawn. The 3D view keeps the WebGL engine for links and physics and paints flat node glyphs, labels, and group halos on a 2D overlay projected from the same camera in the same frame.*

*No symbols extracted*

#### `_gh_wiki.py`
**Path:** `readmenator/_gh_wiki.py`
**File Doc:** *GitHub wiki publisher: mirrors generated knowledge into the repository wiki.  Turns the readmenator wiki, agent docs, recipes, and KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md into flat GitHub wiki pages (Home, _Sidebar, _Footer), rewrites relative markdown links to wiki page names, and turns backticked project paths into commit-pinned source permalinks. Publishing clones ``<repo>.wiki.git``, replaces only pages it generated before (tracked in a state file), commits, and pushes. It runs after every rebuild of a git checkout (GH_WIKI_ENABLED), never during analysis, and shells out with argument lists only (no shell).*
